### 📓 Docs Drift Check
Nothing in this diff resolved to a documentable surface (no symbol, route or SDK anchor derived from **0** changed package(s)), so **this run has no opinion** about the docs.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **0** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 100303c0430eb644506970270a0134db304b7cbb` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

## 席位核对 · ACCEPT · 2026-11-06T05:06Z · #30785

Head-sha: 413f70fd70de8da24616a596f0acaaeae274ad40

- **Shape:** one file, +47/−4, `packages/cli/test/validate-build-gate-parity.test.ts`. Test-only, so `skip-changeset` applies. Inside claim 6677387566 (the full re-post of 6676066855 with amendment 6676114947). Not governed.
- **Cause, measured** (dev report 6677032123): both CI logs time out on the case "the command sources use no call shape this scan cannot read". The cost is the call-site scan, which sliced the masked source from 0 for every match, making it quadratic per file (143 scans in that case). The per-character masker costs 2–3.5 ms and is not the cause. This corrects the premise carried from #30789.
- **Spot check (read in the diff):**
  - The look-behind is cut at the whitespace run before the match, plus 9 characters. That is exactly what the three tests read:
    - `[\w$]$` needs 1 character.
    - `(?<!\.\.)\.\s*$` needs 3.
    - `\b(?:function|async)\s+$` needs 8 plus 1, so that `\b` sees the character before the keyword.
  - The whitespace run is walked, never assumed, so a long blanked comment in it is covered.
  - Three new negative controls pin this: a 200-character comment between a dot and a name, between `function` and a name, and after a spread.
  - `codeOnly` and `callSitesOf` are memoized by source text. Both are pure, so a changed source is a new key.
  - No assertion is relaxed, and there is no skip, retry or timeout raise.
- **Before and after on that case:** under load it went from 8.3–8.5 s (timed out 3/3) to 3–11 ms; idle, from 2.7–3.1 s to 3 ms. The dev also reports per-site results identical over 1914 sources, and ablations A1 to A3 red and restored.
- **Gates:** every check-run on this head has concluded: 48 distinct checks, the latest run of each 32 success, 16 skipped, 0 failure. PR-body guards went red once because the claim still named the placeholder branch; the claim was re-posted in full (6677387566), the body now cites it, and the guard re-run is green. Locally: cli unit 387 files / 5407 tests, cli typecheck exit 0, 48/48 derived gates exit 0 (`--ran`, 0 NOT-MEASURED), `pnpm lint` exit 0.
- **Contract:** `Clause-②: no`, `Metadata-protocol: none`. Nothing published changes.
- **Landing:** ready, then auto-merge, through the relay. `Fixes #30785`. #30789 is the same defect and is left to triage to close as a duplicate (6676085396).
